Here's a description of the line plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between frequency and accuracy, showing two different accuracy measurements. The x-axis is labeled “pop frequency (x10^4)” and has a linear scale ranging from 1 to 19, with tick labels at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.2, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. A green line, marked with square data points, represents “Initial Accuracy” and begins at approximately 0.4 at x=1, decreases to a value of 0.3 at x=5, then increases to approximately 0.5 at x=19. A blue dashed line, marked with circular data points, represents “Final Accuracy” and begins at approximately 0.7 at x=1, increases to a value of 1.1 at x=13, then decreases to approximately 0.9 at x=19. Error bars are present for each data point on both lines, indicating variability in the measurements.
